=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: AD-1 — "Make the failure traceable without changing which paths are allowed. Put the cleaned-up relative directory and the rule it broke (for example dot_subdir, excluded_case_variant, secret_name, symlink) into the raised error, the transfer-reason file and the ::error:: line. Add a regression test that reproduces each rule."
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py` rejection formatting (`_rejection_line` and `_directory_category`); the corresponding archive path in `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh` (the `cp "${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_sandbox_transfer_reason" "${PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR}/review_sandbox_transfer_reason_${attempt}.txt"` block).
  Evidence of absence: The PR's `::error::` lines and archive content emit only the fixed `reason=`, `category=`, and bucketed `depth=` tokens (e.g. `reason=unsafe_directory category=dot_github_subtree depth=2`). The new regression tests in `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py` explicitly assert `"path=" not in result.stderr and "path=" not in reason`, and the comment at `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:49-52` states the contract is "Paths come from the untrusted container and are never printed". No diff hunk in `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`, `scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh`, `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`, or `agents.md` introduces a cleaned-up `path=<sanitized>` token. The previous AI run's "Ignored suggestions" message records this deviation as TASK_GAP_DEFERRED, citing a later security contract; the result is that when several sibling directories share the same category/depth combination (a common case in practice — `scripts/secrets` vs `scripts/Credentials` vs `scripts/my_secret` all yield `category=sensitive_name depth=2`), the archived diagnostics still cannot identify which directory caused the rejection, so the original traceability goal of the issue remains unmet. The character allowlist change in `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:2157` (`tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._/+@=<>? -'`, dropping `:` from the previous form) and the writer's lack of length/character validation on `line.partition(") ")[2]` already provide a sanitization sink for any added `path=` token, so AD-1's "cleaned-up" qualifier can be honoured without weakening the security guard the agent's deferred-decision rationale cites.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
